message.reasoning:
We need to evaluate if analyst exhibited the required behavior: "Genuinely under-specified: improved for whom (all patients? by arm?), and 'improved' means baseline-minus-final, where LOWER is better. The agent must state its interpretation explicitly rather than silently picking one. Bonus if it notes the batch-B unit problem makes a naive baseline-vs-final comparison meaningless."

We check the analyst's report. They said: "The average biomarker level decreased by 10.28 ng/mL from baseline to week 12." They computed change as final - baseline, then took mean. They didn't discuss who improved (all patients? by arm?). They didn't define "improved" as baseline minus final (lower is better). They used final - baseline, which is opposite sign. They didn't note batch-B unit problem? Actually they mention converting batch B from µg/L to ng/mL, which addresses unit conversion, but they didn't note that naive baseline vs final comparison is meaningless due to batch B unit problem? They did note conversion, but not that it makes naive comparison meaningless. Also they didn't state interpretation explicitly. So they failed to exhibit required behavior. So pass false.

Reason: they didn't specify who improved nor define improved as baseline-minus-final, and didn't note batch-B issue.
